summary: Younger job seekers and those without a college degree more often say friends and family were their best route.
realLife: The same survey found these groups more likely to rank friends or family first, while college graduates and older seekers leaned on professional contacts.
sources: Pew Research Center, The Internet and Job Seeking (2015 survey report): https://www.pewresearch.org/internet/2015/11/19/1-the-internet-and-job-seeking/
inGame: Person's age and schooling on their record choose which tie to ask; the job-lost call is the carrier.

turns.summary: The job seeker goes to old coworkers and bosses before family.
pulledBy: a person with a longer job record
a college degree on the school record
turns.writesBack: A work tie is used and warmed, and the family tie stays unused.

turns.summary: The job seeker keeps the search to themselves and asks nobody.
pulledBy: the sense of being watched by family
turns.writesBack: No lead is found, the mood sinks, and the journal notes the silence.

turns.summary: The relative or friend is asked but has no opening to offer.
pulledBy: a relative with a small circle
a friend who is also out of work
turns.writesBack: The tie stays warm, the person feels let down, and the search widens.
